'''Ronald Edmund Dupree Jr.''' (born January 26, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played six seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also played numerous seasons in the [[NBA Development League]], and spent time in Europe and Argentina. After his playing retirement, Dupree was a college basketball assistant coach and works as a scout for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

'''Rodney Ray Rogers Jr.''' (June 20, 1971 – November 21, 2025) was an American professional [[basketball]] player who played for several teams in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]], earning consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 1993. Rogers was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the first round of the [[1993 NBA draft]] with the ninth overall pick. In 2000, he was named the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] as a member of the [[Phoenix Suns]].

'''Rodney Alan "The Sheriff" Buford''' (born November 2, 1977) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[London Lightning]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lightningbasketball.ca/view/londonlightning/news/news_36446 |title=Lightning Make Trade for Former NBA Player Rodney Buford |access-date=November 15, 2011 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304024519/http://lightningbasketball.ca/view/londonlightning/news/news_36446 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]].

Buford played [[college basketball|collegiately]] for [[Creighton University]] and was selected by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Miami Heat]] in the second round (53rd overall) of the [[1999 NBA draft]]. After seeing limited playing time during his rookie season with the Heat, Buford moved to Italy starting the season with [[Basket Rimini]], but joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in December for the [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01 season]]. He then moved on to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], the [[Sacramento Kings]], and finally the [[New Jersey Nets]]. Buford averaged 6.4 points per game in his NBA career.

Buford played overseas for the Greek European giant [[Panathinaikos BC]] during the 2002–03 season. He started the 2006–07 season in the [[Euroleague]] with the [[Maccabi Tel Aviv (basketball)|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] basketball club from [[Israel]], but he was released in December due to discipline violations and poor form.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.safsal.co.il/earticle.aspx?id=7510|title=Maccabi Waives Buford|access-date=2007-10-17|archive-date=2007-10-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071023134934/http://www.safsal.co.il/earticle.aspx?id=7510|url-status=dead}}</ref> After a few months, it was discovered that he had failed a drug test during his time in [[Maccabi Tel Aviv]], his third violation in his career. He recently played for the [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] team [[Azovmash Mariupol]], a team for which he played the 2005–06 season, after being banned by [[FIBA]] for testing positive in use of [[cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] before a [[Euroleague]] game while still playing for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Decision by the FIBA Commission established in accordance with Section H.7.8.3 of the Internal Regulations governing Doping Control in the matter Rodney BUFORD|url=http://www.fiba.com/downloads/v3_expe/medi/Decision_RBuford.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080229162236/http://www.fiba.com/downloads/v3_expe/medi/Decision_RBuford.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 29, 2008|publisher=[[FIBA]]}}</ref> Consequently, he left the team in February 2007 after playing just one game. In March 2009 he played two games in [[Lebanon]] for [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut|Al Riyadi]].

At the start of the 2009–10 season, he moved to [[Eisbären Bremerhaven]] of Germany's highest division [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. On 24 December 2009, Buford traveled to the U.S. to attend to family business. He agreed to return in early January, but was not on the plane with which he was scheduled to arrive. All attempts by the team to contact him were unsuccessful and his contract was dissolved on 11 January 2010.<ref>[http://www.eisbaeren-bremerhaven.de/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=1701&Itemid=1 Eisbären trennen sich von Rodney Buford] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101010072519/http://www.eisbaeren-bremerhaven.de/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=1701&Itemid=1 |date=October 10, 2010 }} (in German)</ref>

On September 19, 2011, it was announced that Buford had signed a deal with the [[Halifax Rainmen]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]] to play for the 2011–12 season.<ref>[http://www.winnipegfreepress.com/sports/basketball/nbls-halifax-rainmen-sign-former-nba-players-rodney-buford-eddie-robinson-130119073.html NBL's Halifax Rainmen sign former NBA players Rodney Buford, Eddie Robinson]</ref>  However, on November 14, the Rainmen traded him to the [[London Lightning]] for [[Tyrone Levett]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rainmenbasketball.ca/ |title=Rainmen Trade Buford for Levett, Add Worah-Ozimo |access-date=2011-11-15 |archive-date=2011-11-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111117050657/http://www.rainmenbasketball.ca/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lightningbasketball.ca/view/londonlightning/news/news_36446 |title=Lightning Make Trade for Former NBA Player Rodney Buford |access-date=November 15, 2011 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304024519/http://lightningbasketball.ca/view/londonlightning/news/news_36446 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Russell Westbrook III''' (born November 12, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Known for his agility, intensity and explosiveness, he is considered one of the greatest [[point guard]]s in NBA history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-20 |title=20 greatest point guards ever: The HoopsHype list |url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/20-greatest-point-guards-ever-the-hoopshype-list-magic-johnson-stephen-curry-oscar-robertson/ |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2996572/2021/12/10/nba-75-at-no-46-russell-westbrook-is-a-mercurial-private-perfectionist-and-the-triple-double-king/ | title=NBA 75: At No. 46, Russell Westbrook is a mercurial, private perfectionist and the triple-double king | last=Horne | first=Erik | work=The New York Times | date=December 17, 2021 }}</ref> Westbrook is a nine-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] and earned the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award]] (MVP) for the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russell Westbrook All Star Selections |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/russell-westbrook-all-star-selections |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2017 |title=Russell Westbrook Wins 2016-17 Kia NBA Most Valuable Player Award  |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/westbrook-nba-mvp-170626 |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> He is also a nine-time [[All-NBA Team]] member; a two-time [[List of NBA annual scoring leaders|NBA scoring leader]], having led the league in [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15]] and [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17]]; a three-time NBA assists leader; and a back-to-back [[NBA All-Star Game MVP]]. Westbrook is one of three players in NBA history to average a [[triple-double]] for a season. He has achieved that feat four times and is the [[List of NBA career triple-double leaders|all-time NBA leader in career triple-doubles]]. He holds the record for the [[List of NBA career rebounding leaders|most career rebounds by a guard]]. In 2021, Westbrook was named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most triple-doubles in NBA history {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/most-triple-doubles-in-nba-history |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA 75th Anniversary Team announced {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-75th-anniversary-team-announced |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref>

Westbrook played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] and earned third-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-10]]. He was selected with the fourth overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], who then [[Seattle SuperSonics relocation to Oklahoma City|relocated]] to [[Oklahoma City]] that same week. Westbrook played for the Thunder for 11 seasons and is the team's [[List of NBA franchise career scoring leaders|all-time leading scorer]]. He appeared in the [[NBA Finals]] as a member of the Thunder in [[2012 NBA Finals|2012]], losing to the [[Miami Heat]]. In 2019, Westbrook was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], playing one season for the organization before being traded again to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2020. After a season in Washington, he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 2021. Following two relatively disappointing seasons there, he was traded to and bought out by the [[Utah Jazz]] before signing with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] later in the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]]. In the summer of 2024, he was again traded to the Utah Jazz and waived preceding his signing with the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], followed by his signing with the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the 
[[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]]. 

Westbrook has represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] twice, winning gold medals in the [[2010 United States men's FIBA World Championship team|2010 FIBA World Championship]] and the [[2012 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2012 Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russell Westbrook |url=https://www.usab.com/players/russell-westbrook |access-date=2025-06-20 |website=USA Basketball |language=en}}</ref>
